countsMean.frames: The sweep's own frame count, asserted by `check-evidence.mjs` against the frames on disk that fall outside any declared `supplementary` set - 740 at this head, and the assertion is the definition rather than a restatement of it: 854 `.webp` are committed and the 16 `supplementary` sets below account for 114 of them, leaving 740. Re-derived for THIS head and stated once. Earlier revisions of this field appended a fresh derivation per merge and left the previous ones standing as though they still described the tree, so it accumulated half a dozen figures from superseded heads and, after the 0.19.5 rebase, a subtraction that no longer resolved - the sibling terms were updated and the remainder was not. Those figures are deleted rather than quoted here: a reader scanning this field for a number should not find a wrong one under any framing. A stale derivation is worse here than no derivation, because this field's entire justification is that a reader can re-compute it: one that does not resolve teaches them to stop checking. The three terms above are the whole arithmetic, they are read from the tree rather than transcribed (`find docs/evidence -name '*.webp' | wc -l`, and the summed `frames` of the sets below), and `check-evidence.mjs` fails when they disagree with it - which is what makes the sentence checkable rather than merely asserted. This branch carries no version bump: `package.json` is `0.19.5` here and on `main`.
countsMean.surfaces: `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `STORIES.length` at the head above - 108 entries, counted off the merged literal rather than summed from the two sides' fields (96 on this branch before the rebase and 107 on `main`, each written by a run taken before the other side landed - which is exactly why the merged figure is counted and not added). `main` brought the model-picker surfaces (11 `chat-model-picker--*` states plus the `chat-session-status-strip--model-switch-pending` band); this branch adds the one story it registered, `chat-tool-rows--trace-gap-boundaries`, and 107 + 1 = 108 is the reconciliation. `check-evidence.mjs` counts the list and fails a mismatch (round 4, R3), so this field cannot silently lag its own source.

partialCapture.note: One narrowed PASS over the slash-completion surfaces - the eleven `chat-slash-completion` stories, twelve themes each, taken with `--only=<surface>` runs against a private Storybook on :6021 - and not a sweep, for two independent reasons stated plainly: these eleven surfaces are the only ones this change touches, and the full sweep is recorded as impossible on this tree (`shell-app-shell--settings-appearance` times out while preparing in Storybook - reproduced on clean `origin/main` by an earlier pass, not re-tested here). 132 distinct frames are on disk, and they are what this field describes: `refreshedFrames` is set to that 132 and `refreshedStories`/`refreshedThemes` to the eleven stories and twelve themes they cover, because the pass ran as four `--only` groups plus a final re-stamp run and the last run's own numbers would otherwise understate it (156 captures were taken over the pass for those 132 frames: 144 in the first full pass, 12 in the re-stamp). `addedFrames` is 0 and `addedSurfaces` is empty: every frame was already declared by an earlier run of the same pass, and the ADDITION this branch makes - eleven surfaces, 132 frames - is declared in `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `STORIES` and counted in this manifest's `frames`/`surfaces`. The pass was re-run and then re-stamped across two rebases of this branch, both forced by GitHub reporting the PR conflicted, and both proved rather than assumed. The first rebase landed on `240fedae0` (`#118`, the send-path merge). That rebase moved nine files under `src/`, and NONE of them is in the subtree that paints these frames: `slash-commands.tsx`, `slash-argument-rows.ts`, `slash-rank.ts`, `slash-token.ts`, `picker-registry.tsx`, `pickers/`, `shared/themes/` and `shared/lib/` are byte-identical to the capture head. Two of the nine - `features/chat/canonical/transcript-reducer.ts` and `shared/desktop-contract.ts` - do sit in the stories' transitive import closure, which is why the whole pass was re-run rather than only re-stamped. 127 of the 132 frames came back byte-for-byte identical (md5) to their pre-rebase bytes, which is the measurement behind 'the rebase moved no pixel'. The five that differ are five themes of `name-list-completed` - iceberg, radient, neon, obsidian, synth - and they differ because the pre-rebase commit carried the OLD frame for exactly those five (768x220, with the board's caption and its roster row outside the crop) while the other seven themes already carried the corrected 768x260 frame: an earlier capture of that story had been interrupted after seven themes and its partial result was committed, so the two halves disagreed. All twelve now show the caption and the full row. `argument-phase-empty`, this pass's other board, was already consistent at 768x300 across all twelve themes and did not change. The second rebase landed on `fb9c0942e` (`#137`, packaging and tooling). It touched no file under `src/` at all - its changes are the CI workflows, `AGENTS.md`, `package.json`, the lockfile and two new dependency-closure scripts - so no frame had to move, and none did: all 132 frames re-captured for the re-stamp came back byte-for-byte identical. A re-stamp was nonetheless REQUIRED rather than optional, because this field's provenance is the tree hashes of `src/` and `scripts/` at the captured head and `#137` moved `scripts/` by adding those two scripts; `inline-mid-draft` was re-captured at `779df65d0` to write them. Every run used the documented `--allow-backend` opt-in, which a narrowed run permits: the operator's backend answers on localhost:1111 and these stories render the popup from fixtures and never call out, so nothing had to be stopped to take them. The provenance shas in this field are the current head itself, so no repoint was needed.

supplementary.source: the REAL built Electron app (`pnpm build`, then `docs/evidence/window-mode/harness/run.sh` with EXTRA_SEED=seed-model-picker.mjs and DRIVE_SCRIPT=drive-model-picker.mjs, headless, 1380x900) against an isolated `local-operator serve` on a port the script owns, 0 frontmost samples in every run and 0 renderer errors. Sixteen states, and they come from TWO runs because two starting states are needed: fifteen from the branch's own seed (no provider credential, i.e. the refusal path — the seed the `before-*` halves were taken under, so the pairs still differ by the change and not by the setup), and the three `needs-sign-in-*` frames from a second run on QA's credentialed seed (`/tmp/qa130/seed-qa.mjs`, a synthetic `openai` credential written through the backend's own AuthStore) — without a credential the owner refuses every switch, so a switch it ACCEPTS does not exist there. The second run's frames are prefixed `cred-` by the driver so no frame can be mistaken for the other seed's. `localOperatorDark` is the app's own default theme, which is the only theme the harness boots into. **U7 round.** The one frame UX U7 invalidated was re-captured on the fixed head and one `before-*` half was added beside it: `needs-sign-in-pick-settled` now shows `This session runs anthropic/claude-opus-5.` (the row the check is on) where the pre-fix frame showed `openai/gpt-4.1`, and that pre-fix frame is committed as `before-header-names-the-switch` — the only `before-*` half taken on this branch's own pre-fix head (`ccbeb0e2a`) rather than on the merge-base, because UX filed U7 against the branch rather than against the base. That run is also the first whose cache lives inside the scratch root: `run.sh` now sets `HOME="$SCRATCH/home"` (QA round 2, Q3 — the catalogue cache resolves from `HOME`, not from the config dir), so the seed copies the same `*.listing.json` files the earlier run read into the scratch home, and nothing outside `/tmp` is written. Both runs' measurements are committed beside the frames (`picker-metrics.json`, `picker-metrics-credentialed.json`), so every number the README quotes is re-derivable from the tree.
supplementary.why: the claim is that a hover, a keyboard highlight, an in-flight pick and the OUTCOME of that pick are perceivable — properties of computed style and of timing that no palette assertion and no component test can see. The unit suite asserts the classes, the transitions and the reading rule (`scripts/picker-feedback.test.mjs`); only a frame of the running app shows the ground and the edge the row actually paints inside a dialog whose own ground is `elevated`, and what the user is left with when the answer arrives after the dialog is gone. The `before-*` halves carry the defect as a measurement: the active row's computed background is `rgb(40,35,24)`, identical to the dialog's, and `before-pointer-left-list` is byte-identical to `before-keyboard-highlight` (AE 0 of 4,813,440 px). Seven of the sixteen states are after-only, and that is the finding rather than an omission: each is a state the old code could not produce or could not report — the pointer's structural edge in a palette where the wash collapses (D12), the footer naming the row Enter acts on while that row is off screen (U1), the band holding a labelled spinner while the pick is unconfirmed (U3), the refusal landing with the dialog already closed (U2), and the three `needs-sign-in-*` frames (Q1). The transcript note count is measured either side of the U2 case — 1 before the click, 2 after it, with the dialog closed 80 ms in — because the refusal sentence is identical for every refused pick and only a count can prove a second one was written. The U7 pair is measured rather than described: between the two frames AE is 85,307 px (1.77%) of 4,813,440, of which 13,230 px (2% fuzz) sit in one 952x64 band across the header sentence's own text line and 274 px are the clock.
